title.narrative: Output 2.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ratify international labour standards

description.narrative: On 8 June 2020, the Government of Myanmar confirmed its commitment to addressing child labour by ratifying the International Labour Organization Minimum Age Convention (ILO C 138). Myanmar is the 173rd ILO Member State to ratify Convention No.138, a fundamental Convention. The ILO, with the support of the United States Department of Labor (USDOL), continuously advocated for the ratification of Convention- 138 by Myanmar, and provided the technical assistance to the Technical Working Group on Child Labour and Workshops with Parliamentarian on ratification of ILO Convention 138. This included providing briefing to the Ministry of Labour Immigration and Population (MOLIP) on the requirements for preparing and lodging an instrument of ratification, and technical assistance to the workshop convened by MOLIP with representative organisations of workers and employers on the draft instrument of ratification. During this meeting, MOLIP consulted with workers and employers on the flexibility clauses it was intending to apply under the Convention and include in the instrument of ratification. Following the constituents’ consensus on ratification of ILO Convention 138 in 14th National Tripartite Dialogue Forum, and confirmation by the Parliament in December 2019, the Department of Labour with ILO technical assistance initiated and led its process of Convention 138 ratification. The ILO also provided the further support to the MOLIP as follow up when the instrument was lodged with the ILO to ensure it was in the correct form. After ratification, two webinars were organized to initiate discussion on ILO Convention 138 requirements with a focus on Light Work as well. Participants were member of the Technical Working Group on Child Labour that includes, Government representatives, Workers and Employers Organizations, Civil Society, INGOs and UNICEF.
